summary: Implement the already-frozen durable webhook capability from ADR 0015 with tenant-scoped subscriptions, immutable queued request snapshots, lease-based PostgreSQL delivery, bounded retry/DLQ history, HMAC rotation, replay and DNS-pinned SSRF controls.

impacts.evidence: Management APIs derive organization/workspace only from authenticated scope and reject client tenant fields; repository transactions set both PostgreSQL scope settings, repeat both tenant predicates and all webhook tables use forced RLS.

Webhook bodies contain only the canonical bounded event envelope selected by explicit event allowlists. Attempt history excludes response bodies, headers and raw remote errors; signing material is never persisted in webhook tables or returned by management APIs.
The previously reserved webhook-subscription API is made concrete and additive management paths are added for bounded secret rotation, replay and history with Draft 2020-12 request/response schemas.

Task 063 consumes the existing canonical EventBus envelope without defining a new event type. Initial enqueue is idempotent per tenant/subscription/event ID and preserves the immutable event ID/type/data in the webhook request snapshot.
Connector SDK and provider admission are unchanged; webhooks are a platform capability consumed by future n8n/developer surfaces rather than a connector implementation.

Expand migration 000020 adds tenant-scoped subscriptions, durable delivery state and immutable attempt history, secret-reference foreign keys, idempotent initial enqueue index, RLS policies and mutation guards with no contraction of existing schema.

HMAC-SHA256 keys live only behind SecretProvider; signatures are timestamp-bound and constant-time verified. HTTPS endpoints are resolved on each attempt, blocked/special IP ranges fail closed, validated IPs are pinned for dialing, redirects are disabled and arbitrary ports/query/userinfo/fragments are rejected.
Task 063 adds no privileged commerce mutation and does not alter Task 017 approval policy. Replay is a resend of already-emitted immutable event evidence and receives a distinct delivery identity.

Immutable delivery-attempt history provides bounded operational evidence without copying secret or remote response content. Full operator audit integration for future UI authorization remains compatible with the existing audit service.

Duplicate EventBus delivery cannot create a second initial webhook row for the same tenant/subscription/event. Claim leases use opaque compare-by-token semantics so stale workers cannot complete a reclaimed delivery; manual replay intentionally creates a new delivery ID linked by replay_of.

ADR 0015 is now implemented: durable at-least-once queue, signed attempts, bounded exponential retry, DLQ, immutable history, manual replay, bounded key overlap/retirement and fail-closed SSRF/network egress policy.

Attempt duration/status/error code and queue timestamps are persisted in bounded form suitable for queue-age, retry and failure metrics. Production worker concurrency, timeout and alert thresholds remain Task 066/deployment qualification.

Migration 000020 is additive and older binaries ignore the webhook tables. Workers can be stopped without losing queued rows; terminal history is immutable and binary rollback does not require destructive schema rollback.

Tests cover current/previous HMAC verification, stale/tampered signatures, exponential backoff, retry-to-success, permanent DLQ/disablement, EventBus enqueue dedupe, replay identity, rotation overlap, SSRF rejection, authenticated API scope and migration/lease invariants.
